title: A result that doesn't match: reproducing someone's image
hook: Same prompt, same seed, different picture. A checklist in the order that matters, and a test for each item.

verified.claim: Noise is drawn on the CPU from the seed, so the card doesn't change it.

All the noise for a batch comes from one generator, and batch_index rebuilds one item when each item holds a multiple of 16 values. Real prepare_noise with real LatentFromBatch matched on (4,4,64,64) and failed on (4,4,65,65).
The batch behaviour in the lab, from a port of prepare_noise, gives the same results as those rules.
SaveImage writes the prompt and workflow into PNG text chunks, unless --disable-metadata is set.
In one-seed renders on SD 1.5: euler and ddim had the same SHA-256. Euler ancestral differed by 61.95 of 255 on average, dpmpp_2m by 20.92.
In one-seed renders on SDXL: normal to karras differed by 23.26. CFG 7 to 14 by 30.99.
--deterministic's help says it might not make images deterministic in all cases.

unchecked: We did not compare the same graph across two different cards. That results can differ across cards and drivers is what the --deterministic help hints at. We have no measured size for it.
How other programs handle seeds and prompt weights. We read ComfyUI only, so a graph from another tool may differ in ways we can't list.
Each difference in renders.json comes from one prompt and one seed. Another seed will give other numbers.
